Precious Metals Quarterly 2011 Q4 

# Executive summary 

## Platinum: in search of equilibrium 

2011 marked the seventh consecutive year of surplus in the world platinum market.  That said, the market is now much closer to balance than it was three years ago; at 347 koz, the 2011 surplus was 60% lower than in 2010 and 75% below its peak of 2009.  Such a massive improvement within a relatively short period of time is a result of both stronger demand and weaker mine output witnessed in 2011. 

- In our view, the internal combustion engine will remain the dominant vehicle propulsion technology over our forecast period.  Consequently the automotive sector will remain a major source of platinum demand. 

- Over our forecast period, we expect autocatalyst and, with it, total industrial demand to continue their recoveries, with the former boosted by fresh tightening in emission control standards for both on-road and off-road vehicles. 

- Since platinum based autocatalysts are now nearly exclusively used in diesel powered vehicles, the increasing use of palladium in diesel autocatalysts, which is being achieved by new application techniques, poses a threat to platinum demand. 

- After being temporarily interrupted in 2010, the downward trend in platinum mine supply that began in 2007 is likely to have re-emerged in 2011.  Assuming that the global economy avoids slipping back into another recession over the next few years, and that the platinum price consequently remains above its cost of production floor, mine supply is expected to recover in 2012 before shifting to more sustainable growth between 2013 and 2016. 

- The excess of supply over demand is expected to rise in 2012 before moving closer to zero between 2013 and 2016, driven by resumed recovery in fabrication demand.  Gains in platinum supply, from both primary and secondary sources, are likely to be big enough to prevent the market from switching into deficit, however.  The final balance will therefore be highly dependent on how investors react throughout the forecast period. 

- The recent steep correction in platinum price that broke the support line at $1,700/oz and went on to breach the 2010 trough at $1,475/oz, suggests that the bull market may have run out of steam. 

- Broadly speaking, we expect platinum prices in real terms to consolidate around $1,600/oz during the next four years, before they again begin to rise towards and through $1,700/oz in 2015-16.

## Other precious metal markets 

### Gold 

The gold market’s surplus is set to continue shrinking over the next five years. Although its size will have more than halved by the end of 2016, it may take a few more years before the market gets to equilibrium. 

- Despite the recent decline in gold prices, holdings in gold exchange-traded funds not only have increased but reached an all-time high. Central banks have intensified gol

d buying. - The sharp rise in bullion prices this year has led to an increase in actual and potential mine supply but consumers outside China have capped budgets for jewellery purchases. - The fundamentals of the gold market are still very positive, and we are confident that gold remains in a bull trend. The general scenario therefore is for a temporary correction before the longer-term bull trend renews itself. ### Silver A weaker industrial outlook has coincided with silver falling by more relative to gold, but a gold-silver price ratio of 50-55 still leaves silver better off compared with when the ratio leapt to 80 at the nadir of the 2008-09 recession. Of course, investor demand is still key for silver. - We continue to believe that economic uncertainty will remain elevated throughout 2012 and see silver being supported at $30-35/oz in that year as a result. At the same time, those risks are weighing on industrial offtake, the forecast of which we have cut though to 2016. - Silver’s price is still encouraging more projects to proceed and others to be lined up for possible development. We continue to believe that much of this potential will materialise if quotations do not begin to fall in 2013-14 and so have price-induced closures occurring. - However, even with a price below $20/t, the market could still be generating at increasing surplus that will leave stocks at the equivalent of over 2 years ‘fabrication demand in 2016. ### Palladium Unlike in our June forecast, we now foresee the palladium market staying in fundamental deficit in each of the next five years. - Palladium ETFs have been acting as a form of supply rather than demand since May. - Autocatalyst and industrial demand for palladium have remained strong in 2011. We forecast further growth in demand for palladium based on our optimistic car production forecasts for the USA, China, and other emerging-market regions as well as expectations that Japanese car production will return to normal levels by early 2012. - Palladium mine supply is stagnating but scrap flows remain strong. The shipments of palladium from Russian state reserves may come to a complete halt within the next two years. ## Data sources and study team 

The historical data presented in this report are based on estimates published by a variety of sources, including Johnson Matthey (JM), World Gold Council (WGC), International Financial Statistics (IFS), JD Power, London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS), GTIS trade statistics, and company websites and written reports. 

However, CRU’s interpretation of these data may or may not coincide with those expressed in these various sources. 

The forecast is exclusively CRU’s.
